blocks.heading: Career Options for PCB
rows: BA Psychology

Open to any stream - Arts, Commerce, or Science - typically with 50% aggregate in 12th (45% for SC/ST/OBC, varies by university). Your PCB background carries no penalty and no special advantage here; admission usually runs through CUET or a university-specific merit list.
BSc Psychology (Honours)

Many universities specifically prefer or require a Science-stream 12th, and several ask for PCB or PCM directly. This is the one Psychology-adjacent degree where your PCB background is not neutral - it is often a stated eligibility requirement, not just a bonus.
The real content difference

BA Psychology leans into culture, personality, social context, and qualitative research. BSc Psychology leans into neuroscience, biological bases of behaviour, cognitive processes, statistics, and lab-based experiments - the exact terrain your PCB Biology and Chemistry already gave you a head start in.

blocks.heading: Neuropsychology and Neuroscience
rows: Direct BSc Neuroscience or Neurobiology
Offered at a select group of universities. Admits after 12th, usually from a Science-stream background including PCB.
BSc Psychology, Life Sciences, or Biotechnology, then MSc Neuroscience
The most common route. Your undergraduate degree stays broad, and the neuroscience specialisation happens at the postgraduate stage once you know it is a real fit.
RCI-regulated MA Clinical Psychology, then a neuropsychology focus

For clinical assessment and rehabilitation work with patients, this route runs through the same RCI licensing entry requirement as general Clinical Psychology, with neuropsychology as a later specialisation.

blocks.heading: Psychiatry Route in Full
rows: 12th PCB with Biology, then NEET-UG
The same entry requirement as every other MBBS aspirant. Biology, Chemistry, and Physics scores and your NEET-UG rank decide your seat, not any interest in psychiatry specifically.
MBBS (5.5 years including internship)
A general medical degree. Psychiatry is not chosen yet - you study every branch of medicine first, the same as every other MBBS student.
NEET-PG
A second, separately competitive national exam after MBBS. Your NEET-PG rank decides whether you get a psychiatry seat at all, and at which college.
MD Psychiatry (3 years) or DNB Psychiatry (3-6 years)

Roughly 900 MD Psychiatry seats exist nationally as of current NMC data - genuinely scarce compared to total MBBS output. DNB Psychiatry is a parallel route with a wider network of accredited hospitals.
Registration and practice
Registration with the National Medical Commission and the relevant State Medical Council. Only from here can you legally prescribe psychiatric medication, order investigations, and admit patients.

blocks.heading: Clinical Psychology Route in Full
rows: BA or BSc Psychology (3-4 years)
Your foundation stage. A 4-year UGC-recognised BA/BSc with roughly 50% marks is the RCI-preferred entry point; a 3-year degree can usually bridge in with an additional course.
MA or MSc Psychology (2 years)
This is where you choose a specialisation - clinical, counselling, or general/applied psychology. Choosing clinical here is what keeps the RCI door open next.
RCI-regulated MA Clinical Psychology (2 years)

This programme replaced the older M.Phil in Clinical Psychology under updated RCI and UGC rules, with full transition from the 2026-27 academic session. Seats stay tight - most universities run around 10 seats per batch.
RCI registration

Registration on the Central Rehabilitation Register through the Rehabilitation Council of India. This is the legal step that lets you call yourself a registered Clinical Psychologist and run clinical therapy.

blocks.heading: Compare Every Track Side By Side
rows: Psychiatry (MD/DNB)
NEET-UG, NEET-PG - two competitive exams
Roughly 9-12 years from 12th to full registration
NMC + State Medical Council; can prescribe medicine
Junior resident Rs 55,000-95,000/month govt; average full psychiatrist near Rs 15 LPA, range roughly Rs 3.4-29.3 LPA
Clinical psychology (RCI)
University merit/CUET for BA/BSc; separate entrance for RCI-regulated MA
Roughly 8 years from 12th to RCI registration (BA 4 + MA 2 + RCI-MA 2)
RCI Central Rehabilitation Register; cannot prescribe medicine
Rs 15,000-25,000/month fresh private-hospital entry; Rs 80,000-95,000/month at govt institutes like NIMHANS/AIIMS with experience
Counselling psychology
BA/BSc Psychology, then MA/MSc Counselling Psychology
Roughly 6 years to a hireable postgraduate qualification
No RCI mandate, but a genuine MA still decides who gets hired
Rs 20,000-35,000/month at school/NGO entry level, higher with a built private caseload
Neuropsychology
Psychology or life-sciences UG, then MSc Neuroscience or RCI clinical route
Roughly 8-10 years depending on the entry route chosen
RCI registration needed only for clinical/patient-facing neuropsychology work
Trackers disagree sharply - roughly Rs 4-5 LPA early-career on some sources, Rs 15 LPA+ for senior specialists on others
Behavioural science research
Psychology, life-sciences, statistics, or economics UG plus a research/analytics postgraduate route
Roughly 6-7 years to a genuinely hireable research profile
No licensing body; hiring runs on research methods skill and portfolio
Comparable to entry analytics/research roles, roughly Rs 4-10 LPA depending on employer type and specialisation

blocks.heading: Generic "Psychology Career" Content Is Usually Written

items.text: Generic "psychology career" content is usually written for Arts-stream entrants and never mentions psychiatry, MBBS, or NEET at all.
Generic PCB content usually treats psychology as one line item next to nursing and pharmacy, without separating the medical route from the non-medical one.
Neither version explains that your Biology background is a real, stated eligibility advantage for BSc Psychology and neuropsychology - not just a vague "science helps" claim.
You stay on the medical route: 12th PCB with Biology, NEET-UG, MBBS, then NEET-PG into MD or DNB Psychiatry.
You can prescribe medication, order and read brain scans, and admit patients - a psychologist legally cannot.
The runway is long and the seats are genuinely scarce at the postgraduate stage, not just at the MBBS stage.
Choosing MBBS-psychiatry only because "doctor" sounds safer to the family.
Picking Clinical Psychology as a "softer" fallback from a failed NEET attempt.
Assuming every psychology-adjacent career needs RCI registration.
Ignoring the BSc Psychology route because "Psychology sounds like an Arts subject".
Comparing psychiatry and psychology pay using one number from either side.
